translation:
  text: 'We began by examining the black stones. They were found just as they had been when taken out
    of the building. The shepherd ordered them removed from the tower and set apart.


    2. Then he examined the scabby stones. He took many of them, cut them, and ordered the virgins to
    lift them and put them into the building. The virgins lifted them and placed them in the middle of
    the tower’s building. He ordered the rest placed with the black stones, for these too were found to
    be black.


    3. Then he examined the cracked stones. He cut many of these and ordered them carried into the building
    by the virgins. They were placed in the outer part of the building because they were found to be sounder.
    The rest could not be cut because of their many cracks, and for this reason they were rejected from
    the building of the tower.[a]


    4. Then he examined the chipped stones. Many of them were found to be black, and some had developed
    large cracks. He ordered these too placed with the rejected stones. He cleaned and cut the remaining
    ones and ordered them placed in the building. The virgins lifted them and fitted them in the middle
    of the tower’s building, for they were weaker.


    5. Then he examined the stones that were half white and half black. Many were found to be black, and
    he ordered these too taken away with the rejected stones. The rest were all found white and lifted
    by the virgins. Because they were white, the virgins fitted them into the building.[b] They were placed
    in the outer part of the building because they were found to be sound and able to support those placed
    in the middle, for nothing at all had been chipped from them.


    6. Then he examined the hard, rough stones. A few were rejected because they could not be cut, for
    they were found to be very hard. The rest were cut, lifted by the virgins and fitted in the middle
    of the tower’s building, for they were weaker.[c]


    7. Then he examined the spotted stones. Very few of these had become black, and they were rejected
    with the rest. The remaining ones were found bright and sound. The virgins fitted these too into the
    building. They were placed in the outer part of the building because of their strength.[d]'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Many cracks” follows the working Greek multitude reading and the sense of both printed Latin
      traditions. The older apparatus reports Athos as thickness; Lake1907 PlateXI line45 prints multitude
      with a question mark. Alternative: “The rest could not be cut because of the thickness of their
      cracks.” The uncertain diplomatic reading does not amount to a decisive fresh manuscript-letter

  - marker: b

      The draft retains the declared working adjective, without claiming unanimous Greek support.

  text: 'We began by examining the black stones. They were found just as they had been when taken out
    of the building. The shepherd ordered them removed from the tower and set apart.


    2. Then he examined the scabby stones. He took many of them, cut them, and ordered the virgins to
    lift them and put them into the building. The virgins lifted them and placed them in the middle of
    the tower’s building. He ordered the rest placed with the black stones, for these too were found to
    be black.


    3. Then he examined the cracked stones. He cut many of these and ordered them carried into the building
    by the virgins. They were placed in the outer part of the building because they were found to be sounder.
    The rest could not be cut because of their many cracks, and for this reason they were rejected from
    the building of the tower.[a]


    4. Then he examined the chipped stones. Many of them were found to be black, and some had developed
    large cracks. He ordered these too placed with the rejected stones. He cleaned and cut the remaining
    ones and ordered them placed in the building. The virgins lifted them and fitted them in the middle
    of the tower’s building, for they were weaker.


    5. Then he examined the stones that were half white and half black. Many were found to be black, and
    he ordered these too taken away with the rejected stones. The rest were all found white and lifted
    by the virgins. Because they were white, the virgins fitted them into the building.[b] They were placed
    in the outer part of the building because they were found to be sound and able to support those placed
    in the middle, for nothing at all had been chipped from them.


    6. Then he examined the hard, rough stones. A few were rejected because they could not be cut, for
    they were found to be very hard. The rest were cut, lifted by the virgins and fitted in the middle
    of the tower’s building, for they were weaker.[c]


    7. Then he examined the spotted stones. Very few of these had become black, and they were rejected
    with the rest. The remaining ones were found bright and sound. The virgins fitted these too into the
    building. They were placed in the outer part of the building because of their strength.[d]'

revisions:
- category: publication_review_correction
  rationale: 'Lexical reconsideration of prior “inside/outside” renderings: the Greek specifies middle
    placement in paragraphs 2, 4–6 and outer placement within the building in paragraphs 3, 5 and 7. Independently
    restore λαβών (the shepherd taking stones) and ἦραν (the virgins lifting them) in paragraph 2. In
    paragraph 5, ὥστε δύνασθαι … κρατεῖν explicitly expresses ability to support the middle stones; replace
    purpose-only “to support” with “could support.”; Retain disclosure of the bracketed supplement while
    correcting the note’s misleading inside/outside terminology to match the Greek and the proposed simplified
    text.; Remove coverage claims absent from this unit’s supplied Greek and translation: the three strikes,
    two-day interval and no-joint selection. Reconcile unit-specific metadata with the restored actions,
    explicit supporting capability and corrected placement distinction.'
